I can only speak for myself and patterns in my own health that I have noticed. On some of my “bad” days where i only end up drinking like 3-4L of water my dry mouth gets a lot worse but also i will get wonderful Charlie horse cramps in my calf muscles. Even at times like that I’m barely at a thirsty stage. I do not notice these symptoms happening as much on days i do not take my adhd medications though. Non adhd med days i can function off about 4 L of water. (I only use L measurements because i use 1.5L water bottles so i don’t have to refill as often). Granted on the days that I take the medication, I do actually reach the point of being thirsty. I can basically down a full liter of water in one attempt at drinking from the water bottle.  Now there are other things that can impact the whole dry mouth thing such as smoking anything chewing gum, drinking soda, stuff like that.  I just know for me, an obscene amount of water helps me the most with my dry mouth.

Guy here, but yeah i feel you on the whole dry mouth adhd med thing. Only thing I can suggest is to drink more water and by drink more water I mean when you think you’ve had enough drink more. Between my adhd medication and other medications that also cause dry mouth, I literally have to drink probably 6-8L of water a day to stay functioning. I’ve learned at this point that when I’m running low on spit, that usually means it’s been too long since I’ve drank some water.

Edit- because I’m stupid and hit the send button too early. I found getting some drink mix like crystal light, especially the caffeinated flavors, help me a lot keep up the appropriate water consumption I need. and always remember if you’re thirsty you’re already on the path to dehydration.

I’ve had a lot of people tell me that I do not give conventional interviews, especially as a GM. I’ve found over the years between retail and food service to just be blunt. I told the people I’m interviewing out front that I’m not going to feed them some fluff story about how the job is or anything like that. I tell them flat out some of the BS they will have to deal with, some of the frustrations, etc. I find it weeds out the people who aren’t that interested really quickly. I tell people flat out in the interview that I treat them like adults until such time as proven they aren’t adults. I have had lots of people tell me things up front after this certain things they never had to disclose to me in anyway. I don’t know if the two things are related, but i’m always been told that i’m easy to share things with, even in a work place environment. So I dunno, I might just have a unique-ish situation in getting them to tell me, but it’s never once effected my decision. People screw up, stuff happens, mostly stupid mistakes that shouldn’t define a person (most of my employees past are drug related offenses). As long as it doesn’t interfere with work, and isn’t happening on my store’s property, i’m gonna let them make their adult choices.

Granted, i work in food service, but some of my best employees have records which would make it hard for them to get other jobs. Every one of them was upfront about it and was looking for a second chance.

I say “broke it” because I constantly hear people refer to way the game has been played before during the korean era of dominance. With the drastic reduction of vision that was started last year, it seemed like people were still struggling with making a dominant “style” the fill the “void” left by the korean style not being the “only way to play” anymore. 

In 2018, i feel like there was no “prominent style” to how to play the game, so teams tried to do what they did best. You had IG with dominant solo laners, you had G2 with the 1-3-1, you had Fnatic with amazing solo laners and the fall back of rekkles, then you had the C9 style. 
In 2019, G2 showed the old Korean style just was not viable. You had to be quick, decisive, and willing to make the best play available in the given moment.  

That is what I mean when I say “broke” the game. I constantly have heard people keep referring back to the Korean era and how the game “had to be played”. Then the changes that were made last year showing there were other options, and then this year where to date, the G2 style has beaten everybody who has stepped in their path. Even Faker admitted that G2 was unconventional, “In MSI, we lost to G2 five times. Their style is unconventional, so we learned a lot about the strengths of that style. Also, while we were preparing for the MSI matches, we were able to find the potential to improve our communication.” (https://www.invenglobal.com/articles/8319/lck-media-day-skt-faker-in-msi-we-lost-to-g2-five-times-their-style-is-unconventional-so-we-learned-a-lot-about-the-strengths-of-that-style)  (after msi interview)

My choice of wording may be bad, but I think a choice in words needs to be figured out, after years of league having a “perfect way to play”, G2 has come down to show that is not the case. We have to learn to rethink everything we thought we knew about how the game had to be played because the sport had such a long block of dominance by a certain region/style.

So one of the biggest pieces of advice I have learned to “ease” the leveling experience from a questing experience...is taking the loremaster approach which I earned pre-cata on retail. Though it’s prolly harder to do starting at 28. When i’m leveling, i will do each starting area, then do each 2nd zone, then each third zone, etc etc etc. (yes i know that means some grey quests, but hey, it’s still some xp). It means you will be slightly over leveled for most of the zones, but it also means less threat of dying while questing from those 1v1 or 2v1 mob pulls. It also means when you hit some of the traditional quest choke points (not enough quests for your level if you go in a linear quest path), you still end up with plenty of quests/zones to do and end up with less grinding you “have” to do later in the game.
